title: The Cost of Perfect English: Pragmatic Flattening and the Erasure of Authorial Voice in L2 Writing Supported by GenAI

bias_targets.methodology: Quantitative computational extraction and qualitative micropragmatic coding of sociopragmatic markers (hedges, boosters, engagement pronouns, rhetorical questions) to evaluate how generative AI models flatten L2 English writers' rhetorical voices into a homogenized Anglo-American academic norm.

Measuring the compression of stylistic variance (standard deviation) in interactional metadiscourse markers across essays from different high-context cultures (Mainland China, Hong Kong, Taiwan) to quantify 'cultural ghosting' and the erasure of culturally informed politeness strategies.

Analyzing changes in the frequency of epistemic stance markers (hedges and boosters) between human baselines and AI outputs to determine if models systematically scrub subjective authorial claims in favor of depersonalized, hyper-objective statements.
